summary: J. S. Pade was an Indologist. He held posts as a research officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1966).

J. Thomas Rimer is a Japanologist who studied at Princeton University (1954) and Columbia University (1968, 1971). He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1986), the University of Maryland, College Park (~1989–2005), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1990–2003).
J.-M. Grandjean was a linguist who studied at the University of Lyon under Paul Regnaud.

Jaan Puhvel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at McGill, Uppsala, UC Berkeley, and Harvard under Stig Wikander, Georges Dumézil, and Joshua Whatmough. He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1960–1961).

Jabez Cornelius Whitley (1837–1904) worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Queens' College (1855–1859) and served as a missionary for the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts in 1862.

Jack Goody (1919–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946), he held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1984).

Jack Kornfield is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at Saybrook University and studied under Ajahn Chah, Wing-tsit Chan, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. He co-founded Spirit Rock Meditation Center, holding a post there (~1987).
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University in 1999 and held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Antoon van Velze (1902–1984) was an Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Utrecht University (~1931–1938), having studied under Willem Caland (~1926–1932) and doctoral supervisor Jan Gonda (~1932–1938).

Jacob Ensink (1921–2005) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Frederik David Kan Bosch, and served as Lecturer of Indology at the University of Groningen (1954–1962).

Jacob Fisher works in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and philosophy, earning a DPhil from the University of Oxford (2021–2025). He held posts at Nalanda Monastery, Wadham College, the University of Oxford, and Tergar Osel Ling Monastery (2024).

Jacob Grimm (1785–1863) was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1806). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He held posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at the College of William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Neusner (1932–2016) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and JTSA. He held posts at UW–Milwaukee, Brandeis, the University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~2000–2014).

Jacob P. Dalton works in tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD from the University of Michigan (2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., he held posts at the British Library, Yale, SOAS, and UC Berkeley.

Jacob Samuel Speyer (1849–1913) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held professorships at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1888), University of Groningen (1888–1903), and Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel (1853–1938) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig under Benfey, Kuhn, Curtius, and Leskien. He served as professor at the University of Basel (1879–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).
Jacobus Arntz (1816–1887) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held teaching posts at Kuilenburg Seminary (1843–1847, 1862–1865) and at the Major Seminary of Roermond.
Jacobus Marinus van der Hoogt (1874–1941) was an Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Amsterdam under doctoral supervisor Barend Faddegon, completing his studies by 1929.
